chunks: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur'at, from Sama'at who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes sexually impure, then he performs the ritual bath before he urinates, so he finds wetness after having bathed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must repeat the ritual bath; and if he had urinated before he bathed, then he does not repeat his bath, but he performs ablution and cleans his private part.'
ai.seo_question: Does urinating after the major ritual bath (ghusl) invalidate it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific conditions under which the major ritual bath (ghusl al-janabah) is invalidated by subsequent bodily discharges, distinguishing between urination before and after the bath. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of ghusl depends on the state of purity at the time of washing, requiring only ablution (wudu) if the discharge occurred prior to the ritual bath. This ruling underscores the practical application of taharah in daily worship, ensuring that believers maintain ritual integrity without unnecessary repetition of the more demanding ghusl.

en.hubeali: Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur’at, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who comes to be with a sexual impurity, then he washes before he urinates, so he finds wetness after having washed’. Heasws said: ‘He would repeat the washing; and if he had urinated before he washed, so he would not repeat his washing, but he would perform Ablution (Wudhu), and he would clean his private part’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Dawud has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from his brother, al-Hassan from Zur’ah from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked the Imam about a man who experiences sexual relation; then takes Ghusl (bath) before urinating and finds wet spots after Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘He must take Ghusl (bath) again. Had he urinated before Ghusl (bath), he did not have to take Ghusl (bath) again; but he must take Wudu’ and cleanse himself properly.’”
